threads.body: The new guidance introduces HTTP status codes but doesn’t reference the corresponding HTTP attribute name (typically `http.response.status_code`) or clearly define the condition for ‘rejects the operation’ (e.g., non-success HTTP status and no JSON-RPC error object). To avoid ambiguity for implementers, consider explicitly naming the HTTP attribute and clarifying the exact trigger (HTTP response present + no JSON-RPC error code/error object).

threads.body: `http.response.status_code` is not declared on any MCP span or metric, so nothing defines its requirement level or when instrumentation records it. This note is shared with both `mcp.*.operation.duration` histograms, where it also reads as an instruction to add an undeclared metric attribute. Either say the attribute comes from separately enabled HTTP instrumentation, as "Recording MCP transport" already does, or declare it on the MCP signals that should carry it.
